A redraw declares whether it was a local edit or a restructure
why: A whole-file redraw can move anything. Without a statement of which it did, the reader must diff the picture to find out, and a restructure looks the same as a rename. This is the one real cost of #vi-sysdiag-grain, and it is not paid by storage shape.

Two outcomes, named on the redraw:

- **local** — the same components and the same grouping, with text or one edge changed. The reader can trust their mental model.
- **restructure** — a boundary moved, a component split, or a group re-formed. The reader has to look again, and the redraw says why.

A restructure is the interesting event. It means a single card changed something that the previous reading of the whole card set had wrong. That is worth surfacing in the map, not hiding in a picture.
